Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
45-year-old female with acute breathlessness, right-sided pleuritic pain, mild fever, and two episodes of hemoptysis today; background SLE on methotrexate.

History:
• Presenting today with sudden onset breathlessness and sharp pain in right posterior chest on deep inspiration.  
• Two episodes of coughing up small amounts of blood; subjectively febrile.  
• Palpitations/awareness of heartbeat; reports fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance over past 2 weeks.  
• Denies smoking. No recent long-haul flights. No personal/family history of thromboembolism.  
• PMH: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).  
• Medications: Methotrexate – dose/route/frequency not documented; last dose this morning.  
• Allergies: None reported.  
• Social: Lives alone in a flat; office desk job; owns a cat.

Examination:
• Remote assessment only.  
• Pulse (patient-counted): approx. 66-74 bpm, regular.  
• Capillary refill normal.  
• Oropharynx visualized – no comment on abnormalities.  
• Self-palpated cervical nodes: not enlarged.  
• No other vitals or physical findings available.

Impression:
Likely lower respiratory tract infection / pneumonia. Differential includes pulmonary embolism or other causes of hemoptysis (e.g., malignancy) but less likely given acute presentation.

Plan:
• Arrange same-day, in-person GP review for:  
  – Chest auscultation  
  – Blood pressure, pulse, temperature assessment  
• Consider immediate chest imaging and blood tests if indicated.  
• Likely start oral antibiotic once clinical examination completed (no allergy to antibiotics).  
• Provide support team phone number for patient to book face-to-face appointment today.  
• Safety-net: attend ED urgently if breathlessness worsens, hemoptysis increases, syncope, or high fever.  
• Reassured that acute presentation favors infection over lung cancer; chest X-ray to be considered if symptoms persist or worsen.  
• Follow-up: as per findings of same-day review; possible repeat review or imaging if no improvement.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: objective vitals (BP, temperature, RR, SpO₂); full medication and immunization lists; recent blood work; methotrexate dose/schedule.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient gives name as “Tracy Chapman,” later called “Doris” by doctor – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational interruptions; no objective clinical data recorded.
